name: Orlebar Brown
why: Tailored swim shorts cut like trousers, with side fasteners and sold in lengths, and the linen, cotton and merino resort clothing built around them; owned by Chanel since 2018.
origin: Founded in London in 2007 by Adam Brown, with one swim short in four lengths and five colors.
opview: “What he needed was not a better swim short — but a short that you can swim in.” — Orlebar Brown, on founder Adam Brown, About page

notes.forg: Swim shorts in waist sizes 28 to 40 and three lengths (Setter, Bulldog, Dane); the founding idea was one short in four lengths. Clothing is S to XXL.
notes.tech: 17 of 227 styles make a performance claim (quick-dry, UPF 50, water-repellent); ECONYL and SEAQUAL are licensed fibres. Thread proposed 2; ruled 2 on 7 Oct 2026.
notes.craft: Garment country stated on 215 of 227 styles and fabric origin on 203, with 96% made in Europe by the brand’s own account; no factory, workshop or mill is named and the house owns no making. Thread proposed a strong 2; ruled 2 on 7 Oct 2026.
notes.linen: Linen leads 53 of 186 non-swim styles — shirts, trousers, shorts (seat_resort read, 7 Oct 2026).
notes.cotton: Cotton leads the non-swim range: Ob-T tees, towelling polos, Giles shirts, chinos; organic and Sea Island cloth named on some pages.
notes.cashmere: A 100% cashmere knitted polo at $895 and cotton-cashmere trousers; a presence, not an identity.
notes.synth: 41 swim styles, 39 of them polyamide or polyester; outside swim three synthetic-led styles in 186.
notes.boat: Concessions in the Carlton Cannes, the Setai, Puente Romano and a dozen resort hotels; linen and a small tab; the deck is crewed.
notes.status: Chanel-owned since 2018, a Bond collaboration, hotel concessions from Cannes to Capri; the signal is the short itself, recognised poolside.
notes.briish: A London house — Burlington Gardens, Sloane Avenue, Notting Hill, Harrods and Selfridges concessions — selling an English idea of the Riviera; Bond wears it.
notes.prep: The tailored swim short at the club pool and the towelling polo after; fluent in the register without the American canon.
notes.surf: Swim is 41 of 227 styles and the brand began as a swim short, but it is a poolside short, not a boardshort; seeded 7 Oct 2026 from the range.
notes.logo: A small woven OB tab on swim and some polos; most clothing carries no mark.
notes.dur: Mid-weight cotton, linen and merino; the swim shorts are built to last seasons, the knits are fine.
notes.golffice: Resort and poolside clothing; no office, no golf.
notes.whitet: Ob-T cotton tee at $145 is a basic in the range; the merino version is the developed one.
notes.comfort: Towelling, washed linen, garment-dyed cotton and elastic-side swim; ease is part of the pitch, not all of it.

cities: 10 stores across the US, including SoHo, East Hampton, Palm Beach and Beverly Hills, a shop in the Setai, and its own site

craft_evidence.owned_d: no — none stated; part of Chanel since 2018, no OB factory named
craft_evidence.countries: 95% (garment country stated on 215 of 227 styles: Portugal 159, Italy 36, Turkey 11, Romania 5, Cambodia 2, "Europe" 2); fabric-origin country stated on 203 of 227 (89%)
craft_evidence.heritage: dated, not placed — "OB launched in 2007 with one style in 4 lengths and 5 colours"
craft_evidence.reasoning: Almost every product page states where the cloth was woven or knitted and where the garment was made (e.g. Garfield: knitted in Romania, garment manufactured in Portugal), and the sustainability page says 96% of products are made in Europe. No page names a factory, workshop or mill, and the house owns no making. Thorough country-level disclosure with no names: a strong 2.
